issues.legal_issue: A court may entertain a constitutional writ petition despite an adequate alternative remedy, and an appellate court ordinarily will not interfere with the court’s exercise of that discretion.
material_facts: The liquidators sought a writ prohibiting enforcement of a tax demand.
An assessment and rectification process provided an alternative remedy.
The High Court exercised its discretion to hear the petition and granted relief.
issues.conclusion: The existence of an adequate alternative remedy did not require setting aside the High Court’s decision to entertain the petition, because the matter was one of discretion rather than jurisdiction.
issues.legal_principle: The High Court has jurisdiction under Article 226 to issue writs for other purposes. It normally will not exercise that jurisdiction when an adequate and efficacious alternative remedy is available, but whether to do so is a matter of discretion, and the Supreme Court will ordinarily not interfere with that exercise. No earlier case is relied on for this principle.

predicates.constitutional_writ_petition: The claimant sought relief from a court exercising constitutional writ jurisdiction.
predicates.adequate_alternative_remedy: The claimant had another remedy that was adequate and efficacious.
predicates.high_court_exercised_writ_discretion: The High Court chose to hear the petition and exercised its discretion on the requested relief.

issues.definition: When a constitutional writ petition is heard despite an adequate alternative remedy, an appellate court ordinarily leaves the High Court’s exercise of discretion undisturbed.

issues.legal_issue: Profits earned in the current period before a company’s liquidation are included in accumulated profits when determining whether a distribution on liquidation is a dividend.
material_facts: The company resolved to wind up voluntarily during a financial year.
The liquidators distributed money to shareholders from the proceeds of the company’s assets.
The liquidators contended that profits earned in the year of the resolution were not accumulated profits.
issues.conclusion: Current-period profits earned before liquidation are included in accumulated profits and are dividends to the extent that a liquidation distribution is attributable to them.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 12 and 2(6-A)(c) of the Income-tax Act, 1922, a distribution on liquidation is a dividend to the extent attributable to accumulated profits immediately before liquidation. The clause does not limit those profits to the end of the preceding previous year; profits for part of a year may be computed in special circumstances. The Explanation to section 2(6-A) and the legislative history, including the amendments made by the Finance Acts of 1955 and 1956, support that construction. The amendment was intended to bring current profits within the definition and to supersede the contrary effect of the earlier wording discussed in Sheth Haridas Achratlal v. Commissioner of Income-tax. Inland Revenue Commissioners v. George Burrell was also discussed in the legislative history of the statutory definition, which was introduced to address the treatment of distributions on liquidation.

predicates.liquidation_distribution: A company in liquidation distributed assets or money to its shareholders.
predicates.current_period_profits_earned: The company earned profits after the end of its last completed previous year but before liquidation.
predicates.current_period_profits_distributed: The distribution to shareholders was attributable, in whole or in part, to those current-period profits.

issues.definition: When a liquidation distribution is attributable to profits earned before liquidation in the current period, those distributed profits are treated as dividends.

issues.legal_issue: A liquidation distribution attributable to capital appreciation from transferring land that produces agricultural income is not a dividend to the extent that the appreciation is neither commercial profit nor a taxable capital gain.
material_facts: The company sold assets that included land from which agricultural income was derived.
The liquidators distributed proceeds from the asset sales to shareholders.
The disputed amount was claimed to represent appreciation in the value of the agricultural land rather than accumulated business profits or taxable capital gains.
The tax authority sought to treat the whole distribution as dividends without determining whether any part represented that appreciation.
issues.conclusion: The appreciation in the value of the agricultural land was not accumulated profit and was not a dividend; the whole distribution could not be treated as a dividend without determining whether part represented that appreciation. The rule in Bacha F. Guzdar v. Commissioner of Income-tax did not apply because the claim was that the receipt was not taxable as a dividend, not that dividend income was exempt as agricultural income.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(6-A)(c) and 12 of the Income-tax Act, 1922, treat a distribution as a dividend only to the extent attributable to accumulated profits. The Explanation to section 2(6-A) includes capital gains outside its specified excluded periods in accumulated profits. Under section 12-B and the definition of capital asset in section 2(4-A), however, land from which agricultural income is derived is not a capital asset, so gain from its transfer is not a taxable capital gain. Accumulated profits are profits as understood in commercial practice; realization of an appreciated capital value is not itself commercial profit unless it falls within taxable capital gains. Bacha F. Guzdar concerned whether a shareholder’s dividend from profits earned through agricultural income was exempt under section 4(3)(viii); it did not determine whether a receipt was a dividend in the first place.

rule.if: liquidation_distribution and agricultural_income_land_transferred and distribution_includes_land_appreciation and appreciation_not_commercial_profit_or_taxable_capital_gain

predicates.liquidation_distribution: A company in liquidation distributed assets or money to its shareholders.
predicates.agricultural_income_land_transferred: The company transferred land from which agricultural income was derived.
predicates.distribution_includes_land_appreciation: The shareholder distribution included an amount attributable to appreciation in the value of that land.
predicates.appreciation_not_commercial_profit_or_ta: The appreciation was neither treated as commercial profit nor within the category of gains chargeable as capital gains.

issues.definition: If a liquidation distribution includes appreciation from transferred agricultural-income land and that appreciation is neither commercial profit nor a taxable capital gain, that appreciation is not treated as a dividend.
